newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to issue $50 mln T-notes to help bank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to issue $50 mln T-notes to help bank.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry would issue $50 million of 18-month T-notes, to be bought out by Bulbank, to fund the stabilisation of one ailing state bank, Bulbank's chief executive director said.
"Bulbank has pledged to buy out the special issue to provide funding for the stabilisation of one weak state bank", Chavdar Kanchev told a news conference on Thursday.
The issue is to be backed through proceeds from future privatisation deals and would bear a semi-annual coupon pegged to the LIBOR, Kanchev said. The principal would be redeemed at maturity.

A Finance Ministry official told Reuters the operation would also involve a buy-back of $50 million worth of dollar-denominated domestic bad debt (ZUNK) bonds from the weak bank's portfolio by the ministry.

The weak bank then would buy bad debt bonds from the central bank's portfolio well below their minimum acceptable price with part of the money and possibly resell them later at a higher price to boost its capital, the official said.
The minimum acceptable price of domestic dollar-denominated bad debt bonds is now set at 45 percent of par.
Kanchev said the financial state of the other operative state banks raised no concern about their stability after introduction of a currency board system due in June.

"Bulgarian Post Bank, Expressbank and United Bulgarian Bank would not face difficulties to maintain their liquidity and capital-to-risk assets ratio. Hebrosbank will need just a symbolic support for its liquidity," Kanchev said.

Biochim Bank is the only one among operating state banks which has a negative capital net worth and suffers a serious liquidity shortage that could be compensated through support from the budget and the central bank, bankers said. @

Bulbank's decision to provide $50 million to support weak local banks was announced by the interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski on Tuesday ahead of his visit to Washigton for talks with International Monetary Fund's (IMF) senior officials.
"International lenders wanted to see a purely Bulgarian commitment to bank stabilisation," Kanchev said.

Under arrangements with the IMF agreed on Monday Bulgaria is to take immediate action to support two weaker state banks before an IMF board meeting in the second week of April expected to approve a $510 million stand-by facility. Under a financial accord with the IMF announced on Monday Bulgaria is to introduce in June a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, the currency board system, to restore confidence in the lev and bring the country back from the brink of default.

Stabilising state banks by boosting their capital prior to introduction of a currency board system has been seen as an alternative to future bank closures, a central bank official said. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
